- Region pinning: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee processing exclusively in a customer-selected region (US-east or US-west). Vanessa / Priyom / Monica — quick internal summary ahead of the call with Acme: quoting Vanessa's message below and adding technical constraints and proposed contract language.

Key technical points (we should bring these up on the call):
- Region pinning: Dedicated/Private = guaranteed processing in chosen region. Hosted = strong routing preference only; we cannot commit globally that no control-plane metadata will traverse other regions unless they accept Private. Proposed contract language: "Customer data processed under Dedicated or Private deployment will be stored and processed exclusively in the Customer-designated region."

- BYOK + key rotation: Dedicated supports HSM-backed BYOK with customer key import and rotation webhook. Hosted can support customer-managed Cloud KMS keys for at-rest encryption (we hold wrapped keys for runtime), but the security team at Acme asked for runtime keys to never be under vendor control — that requires Dedicated/Private. Proposed TOMs exhibit clause: "Where Customer elects BYOK on Dedicated/Private, Redwood will not retain unwrapped keys and will provide documented key-rotation APIs and incident key-revocation procedures."

- Subprocessor notification: OK to accept 30-day notice with an exception for emergency patches. Proposed language: "Redwood will provide written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging a new Subprocessor that will process Customer Data, except where immediate action is required for security or legal compliance, in which case Redwood will notify Customer as soon as practicable."

- Audit exports: We can provide token-level trace logs for the last 365 days for Dedicated customers; hosted customers get 90 days by default and can purchase extended retention. Add example export fields and SLT timing (48 hours for standard extracts).

Attachments: Operational_Controls_Exhibit_v1.docx (I highlighted BYOK and subprocessor sections).

Let's confirm the 10:00 PST slot with Martin. Priyom — please prepare a short suggested paragraph for the DPA that addresses BYOK availability and runtime control boundary. I'll join the call to run through the technical constraints and how we can mitigate them.
